items.note: Usually means a thunderstorm.

examples.en: There was a storm in the night.

items.note: Jeden stopień; dwa, trzy, cztery stopnie (also 22–24); pięć to dwadzieścia jeden stopni (genitive plural).
Pięć stopni mrozu = minus five degrees.

examples.en: There was a frost this morning.

items.note: Pogody is the genitive of pogoda.

examples.en: What does the weather forecast say?

items.note: A long coat is płaszcz (m).
Feminine: mokra. Cały mokry = soaking wet (literally 'all wet').
do pracy = to work (genitive), w pracy = at work (locative).
Feminine: zajęta. Also 'taken' (of a seat).
Poles say robić doktorat (do a PhD) or pisać doktorat (write a PhD).
A woman is doktorantka. After jestem use the instrumental: jestem doktorantem.
At the university: na uniwersytecie (locative). Uczelnia is the general word for any higher-education school.
Plural only. At uni = na studiach; after uni = po studiach.

examples.pl: Po studiach chcę pracować w Polsce.
examples.en: After my studies I want to work in Poland.

examples.pl: Mój brat jest jeszcze na studiach.
examples.en: My brother is still at university.

items.note: The academic who supervises your thesis. A female supervisor is usually called pani promotor.

examples.en: I have a meeting with my supervisor tomorrow.

items.note: Plural of badanie (n). Prowadzić badania = to do research. Badania can also mean medical tests.

examples.en: I do research at the university.

items.note: Both words change: piszę pracę doktorską (accusative).

items.en: to have time off; to have a day off
items.note: Wolne doesn't change here: mam wolne, masz wolne.

examples.en: I have the day off tomorrow.

items.note: From spotkać się (to meet).

examples.en: I have a meeting at ten.

items.note: A female boss is szefowa.
In the office: w biurze (locative).
Female: koleżanka. A colleague is kolega z pracy / koleżanka z pracy.

examples.en: This is a colleague from work.

items.note: To an older man: Kim pan jest z zawodu? (literally 'Who are you by profession?').

examples.en: What do you do for a living?
My uncle works for a big company.

items.note: Na emeryturze = retired. A retired person: emeryt (m), emerytka (f).
For studying for an exam or learning a language use uczyć się.
Also 'defence' in general. Obrona doktoratu = PhD defence.
Plural of zajęcie (n). Prowadzić zajęcia = to teach classes.
Zdawać egzamin = to take an exam; zdać egzamin = to pass it.

examples.en: I have an important exam tomorrow.

items.note: Careful: the imperfective zdawać means to take (sit) an exam, not to pass it.

examples.en: When will you finish your PhD?

items.note: The singular never changes its ending.

examples.en: I'm going to a conference in May.

items.note: Pracować nad + instrumental = to work on something.

examples.en: I'm writing a paper at the moment.
What's the topic of your PhD?

items.note: Female: nauczycielka.
Also czas wolny. In your free time: w wolnym czasie (locative).

examples.en: What do you do in your free time?

items.note: Never changes its ending, even in the plural.

items.en: to feel like (doing or having something)
items.note: Mieć ochotę na + accusative (na kawę) or + infinitive. After nie: ochoty (genitive).

examples.en: Do you feel like a walk?
Shall we go for a walk?

items.note: Obejrzeć (perfective of oglądać) = to watch something to the end.

examples.en: Shall we watch a film today?

items.note: do kina (genitive), w kinie (locative).

examples.en: Shall we go to the cinema?

items.en: to play (a game, sport or instrument)
items.note: Games and sports: w + accusative (grać w karty). Instruments: na + locative (grać na gitarze).

examples.en: I'm reading a very good book.

items.note: Słuchać takes the genitive: słucham muzyki.

examples.en: What music do you listen to?

items.note: Agrees with the noun: ulubiony film, ulubiona książka, ulubione miejsce.
Takes the instrumental: interesuję się muzyką.
Uprawiać sport = to do sport.
Piłka alone = ball. Grać w piłkę = to play football (accusative).
Plural of karta (f, card). Grać w karty = to play cards.
Plural only. Grać w szachy = to play chess.
Instruments: grać na + locative.
Jeździć na rowerze = to cycle (locative).
Running as a habit or for exercise. For running somewhere right now, Poles use biec.

examples.en: I go running three times a week.

items.note: Umieć = to know how to (umiesz pływać?).

examples.en: In summer we swim in the lake.

items.note: Going: na siłownię (accusative). Being there: na siłowni (locative).
A journey is podróż (f).

examples.en: On Saturday we're going on a trip.

items.note: Going: nad morze (accusative). Being there: nad morzem (instrumental).

examples.en: In summer we go to the seaside.
Grandma's house is by the sea.

items.note: Plural of góra (f). Going: w góry (accusative). Being there: w górach (locative).

examples.en: My uncle has a house in the mountains.

items.note: A favourite Polish autumn pastime. Grzyb = mushroom, las = forest.

examples.pl: Jutro idziemy do lasu na grzyby.
examples.en: Tomorrow we're going to the forest to pick mushrooms.

items.note: Robić zdjęcia = to take photos.

examples.en: Will you take a photo of us?

items.note: Agrees with the noun. Jestem ciekawy (f: ciekawa) means 'I'm curious'.
Plural in this sense. Means Christmas or Easter, depending on the time of year.

examples.en: For the holidays we're going to Grandma and Grandpa's.
Where are we spending the holidays?

items.note: Literally "(I wish you) merry holidays". Used at both Christmas and Easter. Often written Wesołych Świąt in cards.
Plural only: urodziny są (not jest). O twoich urodzinach = about your birthday.

examples.en: I have a present for you.

mf.en: I bought you a little present.

mm.en: I bought you a little present.

ff.en: I bought you a little present.

fm.en: I bought you a little present.

items.note: Literally "God's Birth". In everyday speech people often just say święta.
24 December: the main family celebration, with a meatless supper. Accusative: w Wigilię.

examples.pl: W Wigilię jemy kolację z całą rodziną.
examples.en: On Christmas Eve we have supper with the whole family.

examples.pl: W tym roku Wigilia jest u nas.
examples.en: This year Christmas Eve is at our place.

items.note: Genitive and locative: Wielkanocy. Adjective: wielkanocny.

examples.en: For Easter we're going to Grandma's.

examples.pl: W tym roku Wielkanoc jest w kwietniu.
examples.en: This year Easter is in April.

items.en: the birthday song (lit. a hundred years)
items.note: The song everyone sings for birthdays and name days, wishing you a hundred years of life. Also sung at weddings and with toasts.
Plural only. The feast day of the saint you're named after; for many older Poles as important as a birthday.

items.en: wishes; greetings (for a holiday or birthday)
items.note: Plural of życzenie. Składać życzenia = to offer good wishes.

examples.en: Grandma always gives us her good wishes.

items.note: Person in the dative, thing wished in the genitive: życzę ci zdrowia, szczęścia.

examples.en: I wish you lots of health!

items.note: Present: świętuję, świętujesz, świętujemy.
Used for time, not money (money is wydawać). Spędzać święta = to spend the holidays.

examples.pl: Lubię spędzać czas z twoją rodziną.
examples.en: I like spending time with your family.

items.prodHint: a birthday-style layered cake, not ciasto
items.note: A cream-layered cake for birthdays and celebrations. Everyday cake is ciasto.
Said at midnight on New Year's Eve and in the first days of January.

items.en: New Year's Eve; New Year's Eve party
items.note: Accusative: sylwestra (w sylwestra, na sylwestra). Named after St Sylvester, whose day is 31 December.

examples.en: What are we doing on New Year's Eve?
We're going to Kasia's for New Year's Eve.

items.note: Ubierać choinkę = to decorate the tree.

examples.en: When are we decorating the tree?
The presents are under the tree.

items.note: At Christmas Eve supper everyone breaks off a piece of each other's wafer and exchanges good wishes.
Traditionally Christmas Eve supper starts when the first star appears in the sky. Gwiazdka (capitalised) can also mean Christmas.

examples.en: We're waiting for the first star.

items.note: Also Święty Mikołaj. On 6 December (mikołajki) children get small presents.
Zapraszam! on its own is a warm "come in" or "please, go ahead".

examples.en: You're invited to Christmas Eve supper!
Mum is inviting us for lunch.

items.note: Plural: goście. A well-known saying: Gość w dom, Bóg w dom (a guest in the house is God in the house).

examples.en: Grandma and Grandpa have their wedding anniversary today.

items.note: Brać ślub = to get married. The party afterwards is wesele.

examples.pl: Mój kuzyn bierze ślub w maju.
examples.en: My cousin is getting married in May.

items.note: A Polish wesele usually lasts long into the night, with food, vodka and dancing.

examples.en: The wedding reception is on Saturday.

items.prodHint: general good wishes, any occasion (not the birthday one)
items.note: Lighter than wszystkiego najlepszego. Fine for any occasion or when saying goodbye.
Plural: pisanki. Painted before Easter and put in the Easter basket.

examples.en: We're making Easter eggs with Grandma.

items.en: Easter food basket (blessed on Holy Saturday)
items.note: On Holy Saturday (Wielka Sobota) people take a small basket of eggs, bread, salt and sausage to church to be blessed.

examples.pl: W sobotę idziemy ze święconką do kościoła.
examples.en: On Saturday we take the Easter basket to church.

items.note: On Easter Monday people splash each other with water. Also called śmigus-dyngus.

examples.pl: W lany poniedziałek wszyscy są mokrzy.
examples.en: On Easter Monday everyone gets wet.

items.note: A public holiday when families visit graves and light candles (znicze).

examples.pl: Na Wszystkich Świętych jedziemy na cmentarz.
examples.en: On All Saints' Day we go to the cemetery.

topics.title: At the table: manners and phrases

items.prodHint: to pass something at the table
items.note: Podasz mi...? (will you pass me...?) is the easy everyday way. To her dad: Czy może mi pan podać...?

examples.en: Can you pass me the salt?

examples.pl: Czy może mi pan podać chleb?
examples.en: Could you pass me the bread? (formal, to a man)

items.en: could I have; may I ask for
items.note: Mogę prosić o + accusative. A polite request, good with her parents.
Jeszcze + genitive = some more: jeszcze zupy. Jeszcze jeden = one more.

examples.en: Do you want some more soup?

items.note: Followed by the genitive: trochę wody, trochę chleba.

examples.en: Give me a bit of bread.

items.note: The polite way to decline. Polish hosts often offer again; a smile and dziękuję, naprawdę (thanks, really) helps.

mf.en: No, thank you, I'm already full.

mm.en: No, thank you, I'm already full.

ff.en: No, thank you, I'm already full.

fm.en: No, thank you, I'm already full.

items.en: I can't eat any more; I can't any more
items.note: Literally "I can't any more". The usual answer when offered a third helping.

examples.en: Thank you, I can't eat any more!

examples.pl: To było pyszne, ale już nie mogę.
examples.en: That was delicious, but I can't eat any more.

items.prodHint: when someone is pouring or serving you
items.note: From wystarczyć (to be enough).
Takes the genitive: spróbuj tego, spróbuj pierogów.
The food is the subject, the person is in the dative: smakuje mi = I like it (the taste). Formal: Smakuje pani?
Częstuj się! to one person; Częstujcie się! to several; Proszę się częstować is polite.

items.prodHint: the host calling everyone to eat
items.note: Do stołu = to the table (genitive of stół).

examples.en: Lunch is ready, please come to the table!

items.note: Imperative: usiądź (to one person), usiądźcie (to several).
The drink is in the genitive when it means "some": nalać wina, wody.

examples.en: Shall I pour you some wine?

items.prodHint: a toast to one person, informal
items.note: Formal to her parents: Za pana zdrowie! / Za pani zdrowie! Za + accusative is "to" in toasts: za nas!

examples.en: To your health! (formal, to a woman)

items.en: to propose a toast; to raise a toast
items.note: Wznieść toast za + accusative. Gospodarze = the hosts.

mf.en: I'd like to propose a toast to the hosts.

mm.en: I'd like to propose a toast to the hosts.

ff.en: I'd like to propose a toast to the hosts.

fm.en: I'd like to propose a toast to the hosts.

items.note: Genitive: kawałka. Kawałek ciasta = a piece of cake.

items.en: you're a great cook (to an older woman)
items.note: Informal: świetnie gotujesz! To a man: pan świetnie gotuje.
Pachnie + instrumental: pachnie kawą (smells of coffee).

examples.en: The whole house smells of cake.

items.note: Asking for the recipe is a lovely compliment to the cook. Also means a rule or regulation.

items.en: I'm not keen on; I don't really like
items.note: Za + instrumental: nie przepadam za rybą. A gentle way to turn down a dish.

examples.pl: Szczerze mówiąc, nie przepadam za rybą.
examples.en: To be honest, I'm not keen on fish.

items.prodHint: a stemmed glass for wine or vodka
items.note: Genitive: kieliszka. A glass for water or juice is szklanka.

examples.en: Could I have a glass of wine?

items.prodHint: for water or juice, no stem

items.note: Genitive: widelca (the e drops out).
Genitive: noża.
Łyżeczka = teaspoon. Potrzebować takes the genitive: łyżki.

examples.en: I need a spoon for the soup.
